subject: Octant POC: environment alignment, success criteria, and timeline
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@octanthealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Jul 2028 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Octant POC: environment alignment, success criteria, and timeline

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions.

Summary of customer goals (as discussed)
- Extractive Q&A + summarization for provider notes at ~1–2k tokens per document
- End-to-end latency target: 200–400ms p99 for single-turn inference (important for UI responsiveness)
- Cost envelope target: prototype <= $0.10 / 1k tokens during evaluation
- Data residency + auditability: logs retained for 90 days, keys under Octant control preferred

POC success criteria (working draft attached: octant_poc_success_criteria.md)
1) Functional: Achieve 90%+ accuracy on 5 canonical prompt sets you provided (metrics: Rouge-L / human pass rate)
2) Latency: p95 < 350ms for synthetic load, p99 < 600ms with concurrent 6 users
3) Reliability: zero hard failures during a 72-hour soak at expected load pattern
4) Security: demo of VPC/KMS key control or equivalent (if choosing private mode)

Environment options (tradeoffs, recommended path)
- Hosted API (fastest to start): Pros: <24h sign-up and keys, no infra onboarding. Cons: doesn’t meet your KMS/VPC requirement. Good for quick functional validation with synthetic data.
- Dedicated sandbox (our recommendation for Octant): Pros: isolated GPU pool, predictable perf and costs, can be configured with restricted egress and log retention. Cons: ~3–5 business days to provision; requires account-level purchase order.
- VPC/private deployment: Pros: full data residency and KMS/HSM integration, audit logs in your environment. Cons: longest lead time (5–10 business days depending on networking), requires VPN/whitelisting coordination.

Proposed phased plan (minimal friction + meets security ask):
Week 0 (this week) — commercial kickoff: finalize MSA + PO, choose path (we can start hosted if you want to parallelize)
Week 1 — stage 1: Hosted functional validation with synthetic/anonymized data (1 week)
Week 2–3 — stage 2: Dedicated sandbox or VPC pilot with subset of real data; run evaluation prompt sets and load tests
Week 4 — review: metrics review, handoff to infra for long-term staging or go-live planning

Action owners (please confirm):
- Ben Carter (Sales): commercial coordination, scope/criteria owner, HubSpot updates
- Priyom Das (Solutions / Infra): environment provisioning, VPC onboarding checklist owner
- Marissa Cole (Customer Success): evaluation orchestration, prompt set scheduling, success metric verification

Immediate asks for you (Samira)
1) Confirm preferred environment option (Hosted / Dedicated sandbox / VPC) and whether we need a signed MSA before any provisioning.
2) Indicate preferred trial start date window (we suggested Week of Jul 31 — is that okay?).
3) Send point-of-contact for network (if VPC) and procurement contact for PO.

Attachments: octant_poc_success_criteria.md, env_cost_estimate.csv (rough numbers for hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

I’ll follow up with a short one-pager and timeline once you confirm environment preference.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Octant POC: environment alignment, success criteria, and timeline

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data residency / keys: Our security team will require that keys be under our control (KMS) if we use any non-anonymized production data. That pushes us toward the VPC option, unless you can show an equivalent KMS integration for Dedicated.
2) Timeline: we’re aiming for a condensed evaluation — 3 weeks total is ideal (we can do hosted first week + VPC for weeks 2–3 if that is possible).
3) SLA & audit: can you share a short snippet of the SLA for sandbox environments (particularly uptime and incident contacts)? Also need to see audit log retention policy.
4) Procurement: I’ll loop in our procurement lead (cc’d separately after I confirm with them).

Questions:
- What’s the earliest you can provision a VPC pilot given our standard network review? Is 5 business days realistic?
- If we start hosted for week 1, will there be any extra setup work to flip to VPC in week 2 (or is it a separate onboarding flow)?

If we can get provision times and SLA text this afternoon, I can push this through internal approvals and share the PO.

—Samira

Samira — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what I heard on the call. Quick answers inline and proposed firm plan:

On Sat, Jul 22, 2028 at 4:02 PM Samira Khan <samira@octanthealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Data residency / keys: Our security team will require that keys be under our control (KMS) if we use any non-anonymized production data. That pushes us toward the VPC option, unless you can show an equivalent KMS integration for Dedicated.

You're correct — VPC gives you the clearest KMS/HSM control. For Dedicated sandbox we offer a KMS-integration add-on where we can configure customer-managed keys in supported clouds (we'll need a short security questionnaire signed). Priyom, can you confirm which clouds support CMK for dedicated pools?

> 2) Timeline: we’re aiming for a condensed evaluation — 3 weeks total is ideal (we can do hosted first week + VPC for weeks 2–3 if that is possible).

Proposed commitment: Hosted quickstart (3–5 days) + VPC provisioning (estimated 5 business days from network sign-off). That fits a 3-week window if we start by Jul 31. If you want to compress further we can run the hosted validation in parallel with paperwork and network scoping.

> 3) SLA & audit: can you share a short snippet of the SLA for sandbox environments (particularly uptime and incident contacts)? Also need to see audit log retention policy.

I’ve attached the sandbox SLA excerpt and audit policy link here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Coctant-poc-plan (section: Policies / Audit). Marissa will follow up with the formal SLA doc.

Actionable plan (please confirm):
- Option A (preferred): Hosted quickstart Week 1 (functional validation) -> VPC pilot Weeks 2–3 (real data, KMS)
- Option B: Dedicated sandbox for whole 3-week run if procurement prefers a single PO (will need 3–5 business days provisioning time)

Immediate next steps (I’ll take these once you reply):
1) Priyom to review CMK support matrix and share provisioning ETA.
2) Marissa to share sandbox SLA excerpt and onboarding playbook.
3) I’ll send a one-page SOW and the MSA/DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks — I’ll queue Priyom for the technical checklist and timeline.

Ben

Hi all — following up with the technical onboarding checklist and provisional timelines. Attaching the VPC onboarding checklist (vpc_onboarding_checklist.pdf).

Quick answers:
- Clouds supporting customer-managed keys for Dedicated pools: AWS (KMS CMK) and GCP (Cloud KMS). Azure support is in beta and would add ~2 business days.
- VPC provisioning ETA: ~5 business days after network scoping is completed and we have an approved IP allowlist + basic firewall rules. If Octant provides network contact and timeslots for a 30-min review, we can start the scoping tomorrow.
- Flip cost/time: If you start hosted in Week 1, there is no data migration required for the POC (we run a separate VPC pilot). Switching from Hosted to VPC is a separate onboarding flow — we do not mutate the hosted instance. That said, evaluation artifacts (prompt sets, results exports) can be ported.

Minimum information we need from Octant to start VPC scoping:
- Hostname/IP range to allow (CIDR blocks)
- Egress policy (allowlist vs. full egress)
- VPN or Direct Connect preference
- KMS key ARN (or we can create a CMK during provisioning if you prefer)

Estimated infra tasks and timeline (assuming network contact available immediately):
Day 0–1: Network review + access exchange
Day 2–4: Provisioning + KMS config + test endpoints
Day 5: Handover & validation with CS (Marissa)

We will stand up a minimal Dedicated sandbox profile for the trial: 2xA10G (or equivalent) w/ 32GB RAM, pre-warmed KV cache and a 1M token prefix cache for your workload tests. If you need higher concurrency we’ll size accordingly — I’ll estimate cost after we see your expected concurrency.

Attachments: vpc_onboarding_checklist.pdf

—Priyom
